holidays.name: Caps Lock Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for the most shouted-about key on your keyboard. Celebrate by typing everything in ALL CAPS, or by thinking twice before you accidentally yell at your boss in an email.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial, humorous observance that started online during the early internet era. It pokes fun at how ALL CAPS text reads as shouting. It's also marked on June 28.
holidays.funFact: The Caps Lock key descends from the 'shift lock' on mechanical typewriters. That mechanism physically held the typebars in the upper-case position.

holidays.name: National Make a Dog's Day
holidays.description: A day to do something that makes a dog's life better. You could adopt, foster, volunteer at a shelter, donate supplies, or just give a pup extra belly rubs and a very good snack.
holidays.origin: It was created by pet lifestyle expert and animal welfare advocate Colleen Paige, who is also behind several other well-known pet holidays. The day encourages people to brighten a dog's life, especially a shelter dog's.
holidays.funFact: Dogs can learn to read human emotional cues, including pointing and facial expressions, which helps explain why a small kindness gets such an enthusiastic tail wag.

holidays.name: National Nut Day
holidays.description: A crunchy salute to almonds, walnuts, pecans, pistachios, peanuts and every other nut in the pantry. Snack on a handful, bake something nutty, or finally open that jar of fancy nut butter.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It lands in the heart of autumn, when many nuts are being harvested.
holidays.funFact: Peanuts aren't true nuts. They're legumes that grow underground and are related to beans and lentils.
